steps.tx: **Coronary artery bypass grafting** provides superior long-term survival and freedom from repeat revascularization compared to percutaneous coronary intervention in complex anatomical subsets. Large randomized multicentre trials, including SYNTAX and FREEDOM, establish that CABG confers a clear mortality benefit in patients with multivessel disease and diabetes mellitus, complex left main bifurcation lesions, or an anatomical **SYNTAX score** exceeding **32**.

left.title: Indications Favoring CABG
points: Multivessel disease with concomitant Diabetes Mellitus
High SYNTAX score > 32
Complex Left Main distal bifurcation bifurcation disease
Severely reduced LV function with extensive viability

right.title: Indications Favoring PCI
points: Single or double vessel disease without LAD involvement
Low SYNTAX score 0 to 22
Severe surgical co-morbidities (high STS score)
Acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction

steps.tx: The **internal mammary artery** bypassed to the left anterior descending coronary artery represents the foundation of modern surgical revascularization. Due to continuous basal nitric oxide release, smooth internal elastic lamina, and resistance to atherosclerosis, the left internal mammary artery conduit achieves an unmatched **10**-year **patency rate** exceeding **90%**. This durable patency provides prolonged survival, reduces secondary myocardial infarction, and prevents late recurrent angina.

rows: Endothelial nitric oxide release, resistance to intimal hyperplasia
Muscular artery, prone to spasm; requires severe native stenosis
Venous valves, prone to accelerated vein graft atheroma

steps.tx: **Radial artery bypass** conduits demonstrate superior long-term patency compared to **saphenous vein** grafts when harvested meticulously. Multi-centre trials confirm improved **5**-year and **10**-year angiographic patency with the radial artery. However, because the radial artery is a muscular conduit susceptible to competitive native blood flow, it must be grafted exclusively to coronary target vessels with severe native stenosis of at least **70%** to **90%** to avoid graft atrophy and string sign narrowing.

nodes.label: Perform Allen test to confirm dual palmar arch supply
Deploy radial artery graft with calcium blocker spasm prophylaxis

steps.tx: Contemporary percutaneous coronary intervention relies on second-generation **drug-eluting stents** that release antiproliferative limus agents such as everolimus or zotarolimus from thin biocompatible or biodegradable polymers. These advanced stents promote rapid, uniform endothelial healing while suppressing smooth muscle proliferation, thereby dramatically decreasing both in-stent restenosis and acute or late **stent thrombosis** compared to early first-generation drug-eluting stents and bare-metal platforms.

left.title: Second-Generation DES
points: Strut thickness: Ultrathin (60 to 80 micrometres)
Drug: Everolimus, Zotarolimus, Sirolimus
Polymer: Biocompatible fluoropolymer or biodegradable
Very late stent thrombosis rate: < 0.2% per year

right.title: First-Generation DES / BMS
points: Strut thickness: Thick (130 to 140 micrometres)
Drug: Paclitaxel, early Sirolimus
Polymer: Durable thick polymers causing chronic hypersensitivity
Restenosis rate: BMS > 20% due to neointimal hyperplasia

steps.tx: **Stent thrombosis** is a catastrophic complication presenting with transmural myocardial infarction or sudden cardiac death. The Academic Research Consortium categorizes stent thrombosis by chronological timing: acute occurring within **24** hours of deployment, subacute between 24 hours and **30** days, late from 30 days to **1** year, and very late occurring beyond 1 year. The dominant clinical trigger is premature **antiplatelet cessation**, compounded by stent underexpansion or edge dissection.

Neoatherosclerosis with in-stent necrotic core rupture

steps.tx: The angiographic **SYNTAX score** is an algorithmic grading system that objectively characterizes the anatomical complexity of coronary artery disease. Points are assigned based on lesion number, location, bifurcation involvement, calcification, and total occlusions. Scores stratify disease into three clinical tiers: low complexity (**0-22**), intermediate complexity (**23-32**), and high complexity at **33** and above, directly guiding optimal **revascularization choice** between PCI and CABG.

rows: PCI and CABG confer equivalent survival (PCI favored)
CABG confers significant survival advantage over PCI

steps.tx: Heavy vascular calcification poses major technical hurdles for stent crossing, expansion, and apposition. **Intravascular lithotripsy** is a novel transcatheter calcium modification technology. Delivered via a semi-compliant balloon, miniaturized lithotripsy emitters generate localized pulsatile **acoustic shockwaves** that safely penetrate the vessel wall. These sonic waves selectively fracture both superficial and deep circumferential calcium plates without causing soft tissue dissection or distal microvascular embolization.

nodes.label: Advance IVL balloon across calcified target lesion
Inflate balloon to 4 atm for tissue apposition
Fracture deep and superficial calcium, expanding compliance

steps.tx: For heavily calcified uncrossable or undilatable coronary stenoses, **rotational atherectomy** provides mechanical debulking of rigid atherosclerotic plaque. The device utilizes a front-cutting, **diamond-coated burr** rotating at high speeds between **140000** and **180000** rpm over a dedicated guidewire. Based on differential cutting principles, the rotating burr selectively ablates inelastic calcified tissue into microparticulate debris smaller than red blood cells, while deflecting harmlessly off elastic normal vessel wall.

left.title: Rotational Atherectomy (Rotablator)
points: Mechanism: High-speed mechanical diamond burr ablation (140,000 - 180,000 rpm)
Target: Rigid, superficial, uncrossable sheet calcium
Limitation: Does not modify deep or eccentric medial calcium
Complications: Slow-flow, coronary perforation, burr entrapment

right.title: Intravascular Lithotripsy (IVL)
points: Mechanism: Pulsatile sonic acoustic pressure waves
Target: Both superficial and deep circumferential concentric calcium
Limitation: Requires balloon delivery across the lesion
Complications: Extremely low perforation risk; no slow-flow
